summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, interstitial lung disease, diastolic heart failure, morbid obesity, and anticoagulation for prior pulmonary emboli was admitted for worsening dyspnea on exertion and suspected fluid overload. She had self-increased her torsemide dose prior to admission but remained short of breath. Evaluation revealed elevated troponin and CK, attributed to her underlying myositis rather than acute coronary syndrome. A CT scan ruled out pulmonary embolism but showed stable reticulonodular opacities consistent with interstitial lung disease. She was treated with IV diuresis, which was adjusted after an episode of intravascular depletion and acute kidney injury. Her INR became supratherapeutic, requiring vitamin K. Methylprednisolone was increased for a suspected polymyositis flare, and plans were made for outpatient rituximab. Due to deconditioning and new oxygen need, she was discharged to rehab with optimized heart failure and immunosuppressive therapy.
